An invoice is money owed, and its history is append-only — which is why there are three different ways to end one and they are not alternatives. **Void** reverses an invoice raised in error, undoing its postings and refunding anything applied. **Write off** accepts that a real debt will not be paid and books it as bad debt. A **credit note** reduces what is owed, or returns money, while the invoice itself stands.

A pending invoice is still being assembled; `close` finalizes it, applying discounts, tax and available credit, and that is the point it becomes payable. Collection can be triggered by hand and dunning can be paused or stopped per invoice when you are negotiating.

Refunds are grouped here because a refund follows a credit note: issue one against the invoice, then return the money to the card, or record that you returned it some other way.

| `POST` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/credit_notes`](/help/developers/api-reference/invoices/issue-a-credit-note-against-an-invoice) | Issue a credit note against an invoice |
| `GET` | [`/v1/businesses/{biz}/credit_notes/{cn}`](/help/developers/api-reference/invoices/get-a-credit-note-with-its-refunds-allocations-t) | Get a credit note with its refunds & allocations timeline |
